senses.definition: (electricity, electronics, countable) A device used to power electric devices, consisting of one or more electrically connected electrochemical cells or (archaically) electrostatic cells.
examples: His flashlight takes two AA batteries.
His car takes a 550-CCA lead-acid battery.

quotes.text: For GMRS [General Mobile Radio Service], rechargeable packs alone do not provide the flexibility that user replaceable batteries can. For instance, once the pack is discharged, it must be placed in the charger and recharged, which can take from one to several hours, leaving you unable to use your radio until the pack is recharged unless you have purchased an extra pack. Extra battery packs are bulky and pricey. With radios using replaceable AA and AAA batteries, you never have to worry about recharging or buying extra packs. You can carry charged replacement batteries in your pocket, purse, or bag, and in an emergency you can even go to a store and buy some alkaline batteries so you can be up and running again.
quotes.reference: 2010, Phillip J. Boucher, The Complete Guide to Canada's General Mobile Radio Service, Phillip J. Boucher, →ISBN, page 42:

subsenses.definition: (originally and sometimes still, strictly) Such a device that has multiple cells.
examples: Her phone needs a new battery because its present battery no longer holds a charge well.

1749 Benjamin Franklin, letter to Peter Collinson
Upon this We made what we call’d an Electrical Battery, consisting of eleven Panes of large Sash Glass, arm’d with thin leaden Plates, pasted on each Side...
A Turky is to be killed for our Dinners by the Electrical Shock; and roasted by the electrical Jack, before a Fire kindled by the Electrified Bottle; when the Healths of all the Famous Electricians in England, France and Germany, are to be drank in Electrified Bumpers, under the Discharge of Guns from the Electrical Battery.

quotes.text: [For his experiments with electricity,] Benjamin Franklin utilized Leyden jars and referred to several jars hooked together as a battery (after a "battery" of cannon).

senses.definition: (metonymic, informal, uncountable) The energy stored in such a device.
examples: Her phone did not have enough battery for another phone call.
A: How much battery do you have left? B: Only 63%.

senses.definition: (law) The infliction of unlawful physical violence on a person, legally distinguished from assault, which involves the threat of impending violence.

quotes.text: […] A battery is the actual infliction of unlawful personal violence. […] [The defendant] fell to the ground and lashed out with his feet and in doing so kicked the hand of one of the police officers, fracturing a bone. He was charged with assault […] although this was a battery.

senses.definition: (military, countable) A coordinated group of artillery weapons, with any of various numbers of guns.
examples: Outside the ancient fort, you can still see worn areas in the stone where the batteries were once placed.

subsenses.definition: Such a group of a certain size (number of guns and artillerists), within a schema of military unit organization.
examples: They sent four batteries southward in an attempt to shore up the defenses around the depot.
